"Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says"

AT LEAST 72 civilians prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan killed in air strikes, per regional rights group Emergency Lawyers.
Emergency Lawyers, based in Khartoum, said jets targeted "artisanal miners" at a popular gold mining site in SUDAN'S RIVER NILE STATE on Saturday.
"Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented."
Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border.
Emergency Lawyers said the previous alleged attacks represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region.
"The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life... These acts may constitute war crimes." (statement Sunday)
It noted its death toll was PROVISIONAL AND COULD RISE.

HIGHER TOLL CLAIM (non-approved outlet, do not cite): the Paris-based Sudan Tribune reported the toll could far exceed Emergency Lawyers' number, citing a survivor. Eyewitnesses said the attack began around 06:00 local (04:00 GMT), the aircraft firing MORE THAN FIVE MISSILES directly at miners' camps, destroying them and excavation pits with people still inside.
Sudan Tribune also reported June claims that Egyptian forces used drones and artillery on artisanal mining sites in the same region, after incidents of Egyptian border guards burning equipment, torching shelters and firing live ammunition to disperse mine workers.
Days later Egypt's border agency announced a sweeping security campaign along the border against illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining. At the same time Sudan's de facto leader announced an investigation into the alleged strikes, said to have killed dozens.
Egypt's border force said in June it had seized 86 TONNES of gold ore plus prospecting equipment.
Context: Sudan's civil war has driven a surge in artisanal mining; gold-rich River Nile state lies on porous borders with historic smuggling routes; smuggled gold may fund armed insurgent groups and raises concerns about illicit Sudanese gold undermining the legitimate Egyptian gold market.

NOTE vs Al Jazeera: BBC locates the site in River Nile state; Al Jazeera says the "northern Wadi area"/Jabal al-Uqaydat near the disputed Halaib Triangle. Same incident, same 72 toll, same monitor.
